question: Find the simple interest on ₹4,000 at 7.5% per annum rate of interest deposited on 9 February 2024 and withdrawn on 10 April 2024.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total time in days = 20 (Feb) + 31 (Mar) + 10 (Apr) = 61 days.

Since 2024 is a leap year, time in years = 61 ÷ 366 = 1/6 year.

Simple Interest = (P × R × T) ÷ 100 = (4000 × 7.5 × 1/6) ÷ 100 = 50

**∴ The correct answer is ₹50.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹4,000

Rate of Interest (R) = 7.5% per annum

Deposition Date = 9 February 2024

Withdrawal Date = 10 April 2024

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
• 
 
 
 

 Time = 61 days = 1/6 year
 Rate = 7.5% p.a.
 9 Feb 2024
 P = ₹4000
 10 Apr 2024
 SI = ?
 Result: Simple Interest = ₹50

**Calculations:**

⇒ Year 2024 is divisible by 4, hence it is a leap year ∴ Total days in the year = 366 days.

⇒ Days in February (after deposition) = 29 − 9 = 20 days.

⇒ Days in March = 31 days.

⇒ Days in April = 10 days.

⇒ Total Time (in days) = 20 + 31 + 10 = 61 days.

⇒ Time in years (T) = 61 ÷ 366 = 1/6 years.

⇒ SI = (4000 × 7.5 × 1/6) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = (40 × 7.5) ÷ 6

⇒ SI = 300 ÷ 6 = 50

**∴ The correct answer is ₹50.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple vs Compound Interest

In Simple Interest, the interest is calculated only on the principal amount. In Compound Interest, the interest is calculated on both the principal and the accumulated interest. Formula: CI = P × (1 + R/100)T − P.

Leap Year Concept

A year is considered a leap year if it is perfectly divisible by 4. Century years (like 2000) must be divisible by 400. In leap years, February has 29 days, making the total days in the year 366 instead of 365.

Counting Days for Interest

When calculating the number of days for an interest period, the standard banking practice is to exclude the day of deposit and include the day of withdrawal (or vice-versa). This ensures exact actual days are counted.
